newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard says unemployment a problem.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard says unemployment a problem.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday a reduction in the unemployment rate remained the biggest challenge for the Australian government.

"The one depressing indicator does remain unemployment, I acknowledge that," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio. "It is always the last to move, but we do have so many circumstances in the palms of our hands to build a stronger and better economic future, including increasing employment growth as we move towards the turn of the century."
Australia's unemployment rate was at 8.7 percent in March, down from 8.8 percent in the previous month.
The Employment Department's monthly skilled vacancies index, which was released on Thursday, found there was a 0.7 percent drop in skilled vacancies in April.

But Howard said Australia now had a "remarkable conjunction of economic good fortune" that would lead to a boost in employment, including a low inflation rate, low interest rates, strong economic growth and strong business investment.
He also congratulated the Australian Industrial Relations Commission for its sensible wages decision on Tuesday.
"It (the ruling) gives something to the battlers, but it's not inflationary," Howard said.
The commission announced a A$10 a week pay rise for lower paid workers in contrast to the government's support for an A$8 rise and the union movement's claim for a A$20 weekly rise.
